book.dragoncare.bounty.0:
The Hunters' Guild announces a major bounty for the extermination of a stage three dragon spotted in the northern lands beyond the settlements. The creature poses an increased threat to caravans and miners, and shows heightened aggression compared to earlier stages of development.

Anyone who provides proof of the stage three dragon's extermination will be paid a full reward in coins through the treasury of the nearest city. Additional bonuses will be considered for the preservation of remains and safe extraction of dragon materials.
book.dragoncare.bounty.1:
The Hunters' Guild and the Royal Guard announce an emergency bounty for the extermination of a stage four dragon recorded in the border regions. The dragon poses a critical threat to all settlements, trade routes, and fortified outposts. A stage four dragon is highly resistant to conventional weapons, extremely aggressive, and capable of massive territorial destruction.

An exceptionally large reward in coins from the royal treasury will be paid for the confirmed extermination of the stage four dragon. Additional incentives are possible for the delivery of remains and rare materials, provided they are preserved and meet the guild's requirements.
book.dragoncare.bounty.2:
The Hunters' Guild and the Coast Guard announce a bounty for the elimination of sirens spotted along the coastline and in coastal waters. The creatures are showing increased activity near fishing villages, disrupting the trade and frequently luring travelers into the depths. Sirens are considered extremely dangerous upon contact, as they can manipulate the victim's mind and use the aquatic environment to their great advantage in combat.

A reward in coins from the treasury of coastal cities will be paid for the confirmed elimination of a siren. Additional rewards are possible for rare scale samples and magical components obtained in compliance with guild requirements.
book.dragoncare.bounty.3:
The Hunters' Guild announces a bounty for the extermination of amphitheres spotted near the forest and over trade routes. These winged serpents pose a serious threat to travelers and caravans, especially in open regions with no cover. Amphitheres have a high flight speed and aggressive behavior when defending their territory, and are capable of sudden attacks from above, leaving no time to prepare.

A generous reward in coins from the treasury of border fortresses will be paid for the confirmed extermination of an amphithere. Additional incentives are possible for the delivery of rare feathers and magical components, provided they are obtained undamaged.

book.dragoncare.hunter1.p1:
§lDay 1§r

Today was rather warm. I only just finished building this little house. It's simple — there isn't much here, but no more is needed.
book.dragoncare.hunter1.p2: It's only a temporary outpost where I'll sell what's piled up and what can't be carried whole back to the Dragon Hunters' Guild.
book.dragoncare.hunter1.p3:
Either way, I don't think I'll stay here long.

§lDay 2§r

Setting out to hunt today.
book.dragoncare.hunter1.p4: Spotted a red dragon in the forest recently. By its size, it's only just left its mother's nest. The hunt may take a while.
book.dragoncare.hunter1.p5:
§lDay 6§r

The hunt took longer than I planned — the brat hid well. Still, my crossbow brought it down.
book.dragoncare.hunter1.p6: I damaged the base of its wing; finishing it on the ground was easier after that.
book.dragoncare.hunter1.p7: Just as I'd guessed — a young one, only recently shifted into the third stage of growth. Their scales aren't yet very tough.
book.dragoncare.hunter1.p8: §o[further text is illegible; the pages are heavily charred]§r
book.dragoncare.hunter2.p1: §o[The first pages were destroyed by fire. The text begins abruptly]§r
book.dragoncare.hunter2.p2:
§l...y 13§r

Today a fair was held at the hunters' guild. Everyone caroused, drank, danced,
book.dragoncare.hunter2.p3: and sold what they'd managed to bring back from their travels. Mostly dragon bones and dragon flesh.
book.dragoncare.hunter2.p4: But there were also those selling heads, hearts, and even whole carcasses of hatchlings.
book.dragoncare.hunter2.p5: I went to the fair myself to get rid of the bones I'd piled up and to see old…
book.dragoncare.hunter2.p6: §o[The text breaks off abruptly. You flip through a few charred pages before finding entries that survived]§r
book.dragoncare.hunter2.p7:
§lDay 18§r

Learned recently that several hunters were killed by dragons.
book.dragoncare.hunter2.p8: It wouldn't be surprising if these weren't seasoned men who slay dragons by the score.
book.dragoncare.hunter2.p9: Probably crawled into caves and stumbled on a fifth-stage one… maybe even a pair. Either way, our trade is dangerous.
book.dragoncare.hunter2.p10:
§lDay 20§r

Today someone dragged three mermaid corpses into the guild and bragged about it.
book.dragoncare.hunter2.p11: Treacherous creatures — even I want nothing to do with them. Their song enslaves the mind,
book.dragoncare.hunter2.p12: and you walk willingly into their deadly embrace. Mercifully, these devils love to kill the prey
book.dragoncare.hunter2.p13: the instant it realizes it's been ensnared — the mind clears, and you get a chance to fight back.
book.dragoncare.hunter3.p1:
§lDay 21§r

Setting out today on a group hunt. Multi-stage.
book.dragoncare.hunter3.p2: First we have to kill a cyclops that settled near one of the villages,
book.dragoncare.hunter3.p3: then our path runs through the jungle — a hydra was seen building its nest there.
book.dragoncare.hunter3.p4: Sadly, a hydra isn't easy to kill — fire is needed. Lucky for us, we brought arrows enchanted with fire.
book.dragoncare.hunter3.p5: After that we have to descend into an abandoned mine, through which we'll reach the lair of a fifth-stage dragon.
book.dragoncare.hunter3.p6: Word is it's a female, so we'll find not only the heap of gold the brute has gathered through its life,
book.dragoncare.hunter3.p7: but perhaps an egg or a hatchling as well. If we pull this off, the haul will be excellent.
book.dragoncare.hunter3.p8:
§lDay 28§r

Ugh, I hate this work, profitable as it is.
book.dragoncare.hunter3.p9: The expedition was long and dangerous. Of thirty men who went, only ten survived,
book.dragoncare.hunter3.p10: and we all took serious wounds. I nearly lost an arm in the hydra's jaws,
book.dragoncare.hunter3.p11: and then I was nearly fried by dragon fire. But the haul is very good.
book.dragoncare.hunter3.p12: Besides gold, I got a red dragon hatchling — it now sits in a cage.
book.dragoncare.hunter3.p13: After we felled the brute, I happened to find it in one of the cave's side passages.
book.dragoncare.hunter3.p14: Hatched a few days ago by the look of it, too small. Slaughtering it at this age would be wasteful;
book.dragoncare.hunter3.p15: I'll sell it alive. Hopefully I'll find a buyer quickly — I'd rather not spend money on its feed.
book.dragoncare.hunter3.p16: §o[The following pages are gnawed away by mice]§r

dragoncare.config.dragon.max_health.tool:
Max HP an adult (125+ days) dragon will have.
This addon also lifts the vanilla 1024 cap on max health, so values above 1024 take effect.
Set to 0 to disable this override and keep Ice and Fire CE's own dragon.maxHealth value (still uncapped).
dragoncare.config.dragon.wild_dragons_ag:
If true, wild dragons will age naturally over time (like tamed ones).
If false, Ice and Fire CE's default behavior applies (wild dragons' aging is disabled).
dragoncare.config.dragon.tamed_dragons_a:
If true, tamed and neutral (befriended) dragons will age passively over time.
CE disables aging for tamed dragons by default. This option restores it.
Note: the Sickly Dragon Meal item that forces growth is not affected by this setting.
dragoncare.config.dragon.prevent_dragon_:
If true, baby and juvenile dragons (Stages 1 & 2) of different elements will never fight each other,
and older dragons (Stage 3+) of different elements will not attack baby and juvenile dragons of another element.

If true, ALL dragons of different elements will never attack or damage each other, regardless of their growth stage.
If this option is enabled, the baby-only prevention setting becomes inactive.
If true, players get ash poisoning near ash blocks.
If false, the Ash Sensor is also fully disabled — it stops scanning and goes silent, so the feature doesn't waste server or client cycles when you've turned it off.
dragoncare.config.ash_poisoning.sensor_s:
If true, the Ash Sensor plays its idle hum and geiger tracks while held.
Set to false to silence the sensor while still letting it scan and show the level on its model.
Has no effect when ash poisoning itself is disabled — the sensor is silent regardless.
dragoncare.config.ash_poisoning.stage_1_: Minimum ash blocks required for Stage 1 poisoning
dragoncare.config.ash_poisoning.stage_2_: Minimum ash blocks required for Stage 2 poisoning
dragoncare.config.ash_poisoning.stage_3_: Minimum ash blocks required for Stage 3 poisoning
dragoncare.config.ash_poisoning.stage_4_: Minimum ash blocks required for Stage 4 poisoning
dragoncare.config.dragon_fruit.stem_grow:
Chance (%) that a stem growth tick will succeed.
100 = same speed as vanilla melon/pumpkin, 50 = twice as slow.
Lower values make the stem grow slower.
dragoncare.config.dragon_fruit.fruit_spa:
Chance (%) that a mature stem will produce a fruit on each tick.
100 = same speed as vanilla melon/pumpkin, 50 = twice as slow.
Lower values make the fruit appear less frequently.
dragoncare.config.crafting.simplify_craf:
If true, simplifies crafting recipes for various items (Ash Sensor, Tablets, Painkiller, etc.)
Warning: Changing this setting in-game will trigger an automatic recipe reload, which may cause a brief lag spike.
dragoncare.config.dragon.taming.duration:
How long the taming process takes (in seconds).
Default is 180 seconds (3 minutes).
dragoncare.config.dragon.taming.penalty_:
Multiplier applied to the remaining taming time if the player attacks the dragon and breaks trust.
Default is 2.0 (time doubles).
dragoncare.config.dragon.dirt.enabled_ta: If true, tamed dragons will gradually get dirty over time.
dragoncare.config.dragon.dirt.enabled_wi:
If true, wild/passive dragons will also get dirty.
WARNING: Enabling this may cause performance drops as the server will have to process dirt accumulation for all wild dragons.
dragoncare.config.dragon.dirt.speed_days: How many in-game days it takes for a dragon's dirtiness to increase by 1 level.
dragoncare.config.dragon.dirt.easy_minig:
If true, simplifies the cleaning mini-game:
- Stage 1: The mini-game is skipped entirely.
- Stages 2-5: The target zones on the QTE slider are scaled up in size by 1.5x.
item.dragoncare.dragon_brush.desc_0: A brush made of stiff fibers allows cleaning even the most stubborn dirt from dragon scales.
gui.dragoncare.dragon_brush.title: Dragon Cleaning
gui.dragoncare.dragon_brush.press_space: Press SPACE or Click to clean!
gui.dragoncare.dragon_brush.partial: Cleaned partially! Green hits ratio was too low.
gui.dragoncare.dragon_brush.failed: Cleaning failed! The brush took extra damage.
dragoncare.config.dragon.ai_spawning.dis:
If true, wild baby dragons will not flee from players in survival mode.
Note: They will still not attack players (based on hunting targets), they just won't run away.

If true, completely disables all new AI mechanics for baby dragons (fleeing, following adults, calling for help).
Reverts baby dragons to their vanilla Ice and Fire behavior.
If true, disables the natural generation of wild baby dragons in roosts, caves, and biomes.
dragoncare.config.dragon.ai_spawning.mot:
If true, baby dragons will prioritize following their mother over players holding Exceptional Dragon Meal.
If false, they will stop following the mother when tempted with food.
dragoncare.config.dragon.ai_spawning.roo:
How frequently baby dragons spawn in surface roosts.
A value of N means 1 baby spawns every N roosts.
Min 1 (100% chance), Max 10 (10% chance). Default is 6.
